record.summary: Defines 'deceptive audio or visual media' as recordings, images or other representations that appear to a reasonable person to realistically depict speech, conduct or writing of a person who did not engage in it, produced substantially by technical means. Generating such media, or soliciting, disclosing or using it, to attempt or further any crime or offence (such as harassment or endangering children) is a third-degree crime; knowingly or recklessly disclosing media so generated is a fourth-degree crime; fines reach USD 30,000. Victims can sue for actual damages of at least USD 1,000 per knowing or reckless violation, punitive damages, attorney's fees and equitable relief.
record.notes: Introduced on 5 Feb 2024 as A3540, for which the Senate bill S2544 was substituted. The Governor conditionally vetoed the bill on 17 Mar 2025; the Assembly adopted his recommended amendments, which among other things made knowing or reckless disclosure a fourth-degree instead of a third-degree crime, and both houses passed it on 24 Mar 2025. Approved on 2 Apr 2025 and effective immediately. The law does not apply to content that a reasonable viewer or listener would understand as criticism, comment, satire, parody, news reporting, teaching, scholarship or research, nor to interactive computer service providers, cloud services providers or commercial AI developers not deemed publishers under 47 U.S.C. 230. Disclosure to law enforcement, to a school administrator or other advocate to report a violation, or for investigations of fraud, cybersecurity, identity theft or harassment is exempt. The Governor's office said the law was inspired partly by the advocacy of a Westfield High School student targeted by peers who created and shared AI-generated explicit images.

verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026: re-read the New Jersey State Law Library's legislative history checklist for Laws of 2025, Chapter 40 (stored from repo.njstatelib.org on 11 Oct 2026, unchanged on 17 Oct 2026). It holds the checklist (bill numbers, sponsor, introduction, passage and approval dates), the enacted Assembly Committee Substitute (Third Reprint), the chapter law as approved on 2 Apr 2025, earlier versions, the Governor's conditional veto of 17 Mar 2025 and his press release of 2 Apr 2025; together they confirm every field. The Legislature's chapter-law PDF on pub.njleg.state.nj.us timed out again on 17 Oct 2026. The State Law Library compiled the file but did not issue the law, so its quotes count as another official source.

changes.summary: corrected the offences: generating, soliciting, disclosing or using such media to attempt or further a crime is third-degree, but knowingly or recklessly disclosing media so generated is fourth-degree (the version 1 summary made 'knowingly disclose' third-degree)

judgment.status_reasoning: The chapter law says 'This act shall take effect immediately.' and 'Approved April 2, 2025.' Nothing in the stored file shows a repeal or amendment. 'In force' since 2 Apr 2025 stands.
judgment.scope_reasoning: A law that is not AI-specific in form but is New Jersey's operative instrument on deepfakes, with findings on AI 'deepfake' technology; in scope (deepfakes) with no note, unchanged.
judgment.date_reasoning: date_published and date_in_force are both 2 Apr 2025: the approval date (checklist and chapter law) and the immediate-effect clause.
